The Trial Court vide judgment dated 28.01.2002 acquitted two Managers/Senior officials namely, Iqbal Singh and Amrik Singh and two Inspectors namely, Gurucharan Singh and Kharaiti Lal. Rest of the eleven(11) accused were convicted by the Trial Court.
The conviction of the appellants is set aside. They stand acquitted of all the charges levelled against them.

neutral_facts.value: The case involves allegations against the General Manager of the State Roadways Depot, who was accused of selling and using tickets printed on his own, causing significant financial loss to the Depot. The complaint was made by a driver, leading to the registration of an FIR. An inspection committee was formed to check the conductors of buses on specific routes. The committee seized tickets and recorded statements from conductors and officials. The committee's report was submitted, and based on it, an FIR was registered. The prosecution examined multiple witnesses and filed documentary evidence. The trial court acquitted some accused, while the High Court confirmed the conviction of three conductors. However, the Supreme Court found that the recovery of tickets was not validly made, and the enquiry report was not properly proved, leading to the acquittal of the appellants.

They also contended that the seized tickets were not properly connected to the appellants, and the prosecution failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
